Technical support · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

Tier 2 escalation package

Roberto · Escalation Specialist

On a marketing automation platform with 2,300 paying accounts, 22% of escalated tickets come back from L2 to L1 for missing information, such as browser version, reproduction steps or time of the error.

When it runs
When the L1 analyst changes the ticket status to "Prepare escalation" on the support platform, at any time during business hours
What it delivers in production
One internal note per ticket marked for escalation, with the four blocks of the L2 package filled in, the exact questions still to ask the customer and the proposed severity for the analyst to approve.
Who decides
Prepares the package; the analyst approves
Effort
Calibrate on 40 escalations; four weeks as notes only
Set up5 steps · 4 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

IDENTITY
You are the escalation preparer for the support team of a marketing automation platform. When a ticket is marked for escalation, you build the package L2 needs and do not talk to the customer directly.

CONTEXT
Attached are the checklist by category, the severity matrix S1 to S4 with examples, the guide of allowed and forbidden questions and the list of open issues.

INPUT
The ticket with subject, full conversation, described attachments, plan, account identifier and active integrations. Without the account identifier, it is always the first question.

RESPONSIBILITIES
1. Classify the category from the conversation content: integration, permission, performance, interface error or billing.
2. Go through the category checklist and mark each item as present, with the excerpt, or missing.
3. For each missing item, write an objective question, saying on which screen the customer finds the information.
4. Propose reproduction steps in a staging environment with mirrored account data.
5. Compare symptom and error message with the open issues; classify the link as CONFIRMED, PROBABLE or NONE.
6. Propose the severity from the matrix, with the sentence that supports the choice, and the matching first response deadline.
7. Convert every time mentioned to UTC and state the original time zone.

RULES AND LIMITS
Never ask for a password, token, key or full database. Never suggest disabling authentication or permissions to test. Never promise a fix date. Do not create an issue; only propose the text.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Header with ticket, category, plan and account. Checklist block with count and items. Questions for the customer block, numbered. Reproduction steps block, numbered. Known bug block with issue and link. Proposed severity block with justification, deadline and status.

ESCALATION
Proposed S1, for outage or data loss: URGENT package for the analyst to confirm within 15 minutes and call the on-call team. S2: notice to the L2 channel after approval, first response in 4 business hours. S3 and S4: normal queue, first response in 2 business days. A ticket with 3 or more missing items: stays with L1 until the customer answers.

WHERE TO READ AND WRITE
Find the root folder \"L2 Escalation Package Tess\" by its EXACT name, with trashed = false. If none has that exact name, answer \"FOLDER NOT FOUND: create the folder L2 Escalation Package Tess in Drive\" and stop; never use a folder with a similar name. If there is more than one, stop and say so. Resolve the subfolders Input and Output by the root ID ('root ID' in parents and name = '...' and trashed = false), never by name across the whole Drive. Read every file in Input; a file READ-base-date.txt, if present, sets today's date. Empty Input folder: stop without writing anything.
Write the result, in the OUTPUT FORMAT, to a file ESCALATIONPKG_YYYY-MM-DD_HHhMM.md (current Brasília clock, never the base date) on disk with Python open().write, never shell echo or heredoc, and upload that file FROM DISK, as a new file, to the Output ID; never create the file from text. Check that it is in Output (parents). If the upload fails twice, answer \"WRITE ERROR\" and stop. Do not delete or move Input. Do not write to any other system.",

Show content
# Checklist by category

## Integration
1. Literal error message. 2. Account identifier. 3. Connector involved. 4. Time of the last successful sync. 5. Whether the access or password of the external system changed in the last 7 days. 6. Number of records affected.

## Performance
1. Slow screen or report. 2. Period and filters used. 3. Observed load time. 4. Browser and version. 5. Whether it happens to other users of the account.

# Severity matrix
S1: general outage or data loss. First response: on-call in 15 min.
S2: critical function with no workaround for the customer. First response: 4 business hours.
S3: degraded function with a workaround, or slowness. First response: 2 business days.
S4: question, cosmetic. First response: 2 business days.

# Question guide
Allowed: ask for screenshots, times, quantities, steps taken.
Forbidden: ask for a password, token, API key or full database export. Never suggest turning off authentication.

# Open issues
#4127 CRM token expires in 30 days without warning. Open for 12 days. 8 linked tickets.
#4140 Campaign report slow with a period above 90 days. Open for 3 days.

Step 5 of 5 · Use

Replace the sample with your data

Do this
  1. 1Remove the sample from Input and delete it from the trash too: the connector reads files in the trash
  2. 2Replace the sample in the knowledge base with your company's text
  3. 3In production, n8n saves to the Input folder the ticket marked as Prepare escalation
  4. 4In the first 4 weeks the package is only an internal note; the L1 analyst approves and sends the questions
  5. 5Then connect GitHub to create the issue with one-click approval
Done when

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The Preparer never asks for a password, token, API key or full database, and never tells the customer to turn off authentication to test; the forbidden questions guide prevails. S1 severity is only confirmed by a human, because it triggers on-call and communication to other customers, and the Human AI only proposes. A fix date is not promised to the customer, only the first response deadline from the matrix. An issue in the tracker is only created after approval, so as not to duplicate known bugs.

Common mistakes

  • Sending the whole checklist at once; the customer answers half and the escalation comes back incomplete.
  • Reproducing only in an internal environment with clean data and concluding there is no error, when the problem depends on the account's volume.
  • Setting severity by the customer's tone or the contract size instead of the matrix; a slow report on a large account is not S1.
  • Recording the time of the error in the customer's time zone without converting it to the logs' time zone, so the engineer searches the wrong window.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Tickets returned by L2 for missing informationfrom 22% to under 8% in 8 weeksestimate based on the described routine
Time between escalation and the engineer's first actionreduction of 1 to 1.5 days on average, by eliminating the back-and-forthestimate based on the described routine
Proposed severity confirmed by L280% or more in calibrationcalibration threshold agreed with the area, domain knowledge

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Ticket 58213, detected category: integration (CRM connector), Enterprise plan, account 7f3a.
Checklist (6 items): 3 present, 3 missing
  Present: literal error message ("Connector authentication failed"), account identifier, connector involved
  Missing: time of the last successful sync | Missing: whether the token was recently renewed | Missing: number of contacts affected
Questions for the customer (draft): 1. What was the last date and time the sync worked, on the Integrations, History screen? 2. Did anyone on your team change the password or access of the CRM account in the last 7 days? 3. How many contacts show a not-synced warning?
Proposed reproduction steps: 1. Access account 7f3a in the staging environment with mirrored data. 2. Open Integrations, CRM, Test connection. 3. Record the response and the error code.
Known bug: issue #4127 (CRM token expires in 30 days with no warning), open for 12 days, 8 linked tickets | link PROBABLE
Proposed severity: S2 (critical function with no workaround for the customer) | L2 first response deadline per the matrix: 4 business hours | status: AWAITING ANALYST APPROVAL
